title: Synthesis --- The Gift and the Motive

lessons.title: Synthesis — the gift and the motive
lessons.gloss: synthesis — a short exchange in which the two-letter difference changes what one person means to another

segments.text: Para ti or por ti — one of them is a present and one of them is a reason. Which is which?
Read this twice, changing only one word.
— Hago la comida para ti. — Gracias.
The first is somebody cooking you dinner. The second is somebody telling you they are cooking because of you — which, depending on the day, is an act of love or a small complaint.
Two letters. Nothing else in the sentence moved.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: a preposition carrying the feeling

segments.text: This is the first place in the book where the smallest word in the sentence carries its emotional content.

Nouns and verbs have been doing the meaning until now. Here the noun is the same, the verb is the same, the person is the same — and the sentence changes completely on a preposition. That is worth meeting deliberately, because English speakers arrive expecting the little words to be plumbing.

They are not plumbing here. Por and para are the difference between I made this for you and I made this because of you, and no amount of context repairs the wrong one: your listener will simply hear the thing you did not mean.

Which is also the reassuring part. If you pick the wrong one, you have not produced nonsense or bad grammar — you have said something true about a different situation. Somebody will look faintly puzzled, and you will notice, and that is how this stops being difficult.

segments.instruction: both versions of the dinner sentence, and hear the second one land differently
segments.source: [YOU SAY: both versions of the dinner sentence, and hear the second one land differently]

segments.prompt: Tell somebody you are making the meal as a gift to them.
Now say it meaning they are the reason you are doing it at all.

feedback.correct: Love or complaint, depending on the day.
Por — the cause of your thanks.

segments.prompt: You pick the wrong one of the two. What have you produced?
acceptedResponses: a true sentence about a different situation
something correct that means something else
not nonsense, just the wrong meaning

feedback.correct: Which is why this stops being difficult once you are talking to people.
feedback.incorrect: Not bad grammar — a perfectly good sentence about something you did not mean.

segments.text: Para ti — a gift or a reason? (A gift.) Por ti? (A reason.) And what happens if you choose wrong? (You say something true about a different situation — and somebody will look puzzled, which is how you learn it.)
